subject: Oceanography
title: Life in the Blue Desert
description: One-minute skill: Life in the Blue Desert.

hook.text: The open ocean covers 60% of Earth's surface—yet it is often called a biological desert.

buildup.text: Far from coasts and upwelling zones, nutrients are scarce—phytoplankton are sparse.

discovery.text: Life concentrates around floating objects, fronts, and eddies—any structure in the vast blue void.

twist.text: Despite low density, the open ocean's sheer size means it produces more total biomass than all coasts combined.

climax.text: Tuna, sharks, and seabirds patrol these waters—covering enormous distances to find food.

punchline.text: The emptiest ocean still outproduces the busiest coast.

quiz.question: Why is the open ocean called a 'biological desert'?
options: Nutrients are scarce, making life sparse per unit area
It is too cold for life
